actions.title: Pick one sustainable habit to add this week
actions.desc: Choose something small and specific — like bringing a bag to the shops or switching off standby devices before bed. Attach it to something you already do every day.

actions.title: Do a 10-minute home energy audit
actions.desc: Walk around your home and note anything that uses energy unnecessarily — old bulbs, devices on standby, gaps in doors or windows. Most fixes take minutes.
actions.impact: Up to 100 kg CO₂/year if acted on

actions.title: Plan one meat-free day per week for April
actions.desc: Commit to one full day each week without meat for the month. That alone could save around 50–100 kg CO₂ over the month.

actions.title: Check one climate 'fact' you believe and verify it
actions.desc: Pick something you think you know about climate and look it up on Our World in Data or the EPA Ireland site. You might be surprised.

actions.title: Share one surprising fact with someone today
actions.desc: Pick the most surprising thing you learned in this quiz and mention it to one person. Research shows peer conversations are more effective than media campaigns at shifting views.

actions.title: Spend 30 minutes outside in a green space this week
actions.desc: It doesn't have to be wild — a local park counts. Leave the headphones behind if you can and just notice what's around you.

actions.title: Let a patch of your garden or windowsill go wild
actions.desc: Stop cutting one corner of the lawn, or plant a small pot of wildflowers on your windowsill. Even tiny wild patches support pollinators in urban areas.

actions.title: Check the sustainability rating of your fish today
actions.desc: The Good Fish Guide by the Marine Conservation Society rates fish by sustainability. Check goodfishguide.org before you buy fish this week.

actions.title: Try mackerel, mussels or sardines this week
actions.desc: These are among the most sustainable and nutritious seafood options in Ireland — and usually cheaper than salmon or tuna. Tinned works just as well.

actions.title: Download the iNaturalist app and log one species this week
actions.desc: iNaturalist is free and lets you photograph plants, birds or insects and have them identified automatically. Every observation contributes to national biodiversity data.

actions.title: Plant one native Irish wildflower this spring
actions.desc: Primrose, cowslip, wild garlic or ox-eye daisy are all easy to grow in pots or gardens and support native insects. Most garden centres stock them from April.

actions.title: Fix a dripping tap at home this week
actions.desc: A dripping tap wastes up to 15 litres a day — that's over 5,000 litres a year. Most fixes take 10 minutes and cost very little.

actions.title: Eat one less portion of beef this week
actions.desc: Replacing one beef meal with chicken, fish or legumes saves not just carbon but a significant amount of embedded water.

actions.title: Go for a hedgerow walk and identify 3 species
actions.desc: Use the free iNaturalist or PlantNet app to identify what's growing in a local hedgerow. Hawthorn, blackthorn and elder are the most common in Ireland.

actions.title: Plant a native Irish hedgerow plant in your garden
actions.desc: Hawthorn, blackthorn or hazel are all cheap, fast-growing and excellent for wildlife. Even a single plant in a garden makes a difference for birds and insects.

actions.title: Take a 20-minute walk outside without your phone this week
actions.desc: Leave the podcast and headphones behind just once. Walk somewhere green if you can — a park, a canal path, a beach. Notice what you see, hear and smell.

actions.title: Suggest a walking meeting at work this week
actions.desc: Replace one sit-down meeting with a walk-and-talk outside. It's better for creativity, better for wellbeing, and uses no energy.

actions.title: If you're going to a festival this summer, plan to travel by public transport
actions.desc: Most major Irish festivals are served by shuttle buses or trains. Check the transport options now and book early — it's usually cheaper and takes the parking stress away.
actions.impact: Could save 20–50 kg CO₂ vs driving alone

actions.title: Pack a festival kit that cuts waste
actions.desc: Reusable cup, water bottle, solid shampoo bar, and a bag for sorting recycling. Most of this costs nothing if you already have it.

actions.title: Take part in a Clean Coasts beach clean this month
actions.desc: Clean Coasts Ireland runs regular community beach cleans around the whole coast. Find one at cleancoasts.org — they provide bags and gloves.

actions.title: Switch to a plastic-free shampoo or soap bar
actions.desc: Shampoo bars last 2–3x longer than bottled versions and avoid the plastic entirely. Several Irish brands now make them.

actions.title: Find one piece of art, music or writing about nature or climate this week
actions.desc: A poem, a documentary, an album, a painting — it doesn't matter. Notice how it makes you feel. Art reaches the parts that facts sometimes can't.
actions.impact: Builds emotional connection to the issue

actions.title: Support an Irish environmental arts project
actions.desc: Look up Commonage, Phizzfest or similar Irish environmental arts programmes. Even sharing their work on social media helps build the audience for climate culture.

actions.title: Have one climate conversation this week — without lecturing
actions.desc: Start by asking someone what they think about something local — the weather, food prices, a nature story in the news. Listen first. Share one surprising fact if it feels natural.

actions.title: Share one thing you learned today on social media or WhatsApp
actions.desc: Even a short message or forwarding this quiz to one person breaks the spiral of silence. You don't need to be an expert — just curious.

actions.title: Check if your home energy provider offers a green tariff
actions.desc: Many Irish energy suppliers now offer tariffs where your electricity is matched to renewable generation. Switching can take less than 10 minutes online.

actions.title: Calculate your carbon footprint today
actions.desc: Use a free online calculator — try myclimate.org or the WWF footprint calculator. It takes 5 minutes and shows where your biggest impact areas are.

actions.title: Commit to one meat-free day per week
actions.desc: Switching one day per week from meat to plant-based food is one of the highest-impact individual diet changes. Try it for April first.

actions.title: Talk to 3 people about climate action this week
actions.desc: Share what you learned today. Research shows social norms shift when people talk openly about behaviour change — and most people are more open than you'd expect.

actions.title: Add one climate or nature book to your reading list
actions.desc: Try 'Braiding Sweetgrass' by Robin Wall Kimmerer, 'Feral' by George Monbiot, or 'How to Avoid a Climate Disaster' by Bill Gates. Your local library will likely have at least one.

actions.title: Listen to one episode of a climate or nature podcast this week
actions.desc: Try 'How to Save a Planet', 'Outrage + Optimism', or 'The Irish Times Climate Podcast'. Even one episode can shift how you think about the issue.

actions.title: Plant a tree — or fund one being planted
actions.desc: Native Irish trees like oak, birch, hazel or rowan. If you don't have a garden, organisations like Easy Treesie or Native Woodland Trust plant on your behalf.

actions.title: Choose wood products with FSC certification
actions.desc: The Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) label means timber came from responsibly managed forests. Look for it on paper, furniture and wood products — widely available in Irish shops.

actions.title: Repair something instead of replacing it this week
actions.desc: A torn bag, a broken button, a cracked phone case — look up a repair tutorial before buying a replacement. Repair Cafés operate in most Irish cities and are free to attend.
actions.impact: Extends product life, avoids manufacturing emissions

actions.title: Declutter one drawer or shelf and donate or sell what you don't use
actions.desc: Donating to charity shops, selling on Done Deal or giving away on Buy Nothing groups keeps items in circulation and out of landfill.

actions.title: Suggest one green initiative at your workplace this week
actions.desc: It could be as simple as asking about switching to a green energy tariff, starting a composting scheme, or setting up a lunchtime walking group.

actions.title: Swap one car commute for walking, cycling or public transport
actions.desc: Even one day per week makes a difference. Most Irish cities now have Bike to Work schemes and Leap card subsidies through employers.

actions.title: Do a fridge audit before your next food shop
actions.desc: Before you go shopping this week, check what's already in your fridge and cupboards. Write a list based on what you actually need. Stick to it.

actions.title: Try one 'use it up' meal this week
actions.desc: Cook one meal entirely from what's already in the fridge and cupboards — no new shopping. It's often surprisingly good and saves money and waste.

actions.title: Download the Too Good To Go app
actions.desc: Too Good To Go lets you buy surplus food from local restaurants, cafés and supermarkets at a fraction of the price. Available in Dublin, Cork, Galway and many other Irish towns.

actions.title: Create a quiet hour at home this evening — no screens, no background noise
actions.desc: Turn off the TV and music for one hour. Read, cook, chat or sit outside. Notice how your body responds to the quiet.

actions.title: Walk or cycle instead of driving for one short trip this week
actions.desc: Every car journey replaced by walking or cycling removes noise, reduces air pollution, cuts carbon and is good for your health.

actions.title: Check if your employer is signed up to the Bike to Work scheme
actions.desc: Visit biketowork.ie — it takes 5 minutes. The scheme saves you up to 52% on a new bike through salary sacrifice.

actions.title: Try cycling or walking for one short trip this week instead of driving
actions.desc: Any trip under 3km is faster by bike in most Irish towns once you factor in parking. Give it one try this week.

actions.title: Check your home's BER rating
actions.desc: Visit seai.ie — it is free and shows where you lose most heat and energy. A poor BER means higher bills and higher emissions.
actions.impact: Awareness step — improving BER can cut emissions by up to 50%

actions.title: Cook one traditional Irish plant-based meal this week
actions.desc: Colcannon, vegetable soup, or oat porridge — simple, cheap and very low carbon. The traditional Irish diet was ahead of its time.
actions.impact: Plant-based meals save 1–3 kg CO₂ vs meat equivalent

actions.title: Buy one Irish-grown vegetable this week instead of an imported one
actions.desc: Check the label — Irish-grown carrots, cabbage, leeks and potatoes are widely available in all supermarkets. Supporting local reduces food miles and keeps Irish farming land productive.
actions.impact: Reduces food miles and supports Irish land use

actions.title: Plan one outdoor walk this weekend using the Trails Ireland app
actions.desc: The Trails Ireland app is free and lists thousands of walks across the country by location, distance and difficulty. Find one near you and go.

actions.title: Swap one gym session for an outdoor run or walk this week
actions.desc: Outdoor exercise has been shown to have greater mental health benefits than the same exercise indoors — and it uses no energy.
actions.impact: Saves gym energy use + connects you to local nature

actions.title: Repair something this week instead of replacing it
actions.desc: A torn bag, a broken button, a cracked phone case — look up a repair tutorial on YouTube before buying a replacement. Repair Cafés operate in most Irish cities and are free. Find one at repaircafe.ie.
actions.impact: Extends product life and avoids manufacturing emissions

actions.title: Cook one meal entirely from what is already in your fridge and cupboards
actions.desc: Before your next shop, cook once using only what you already have. It is usually cheaper, wastes nothing and is often surprisingly good.
actions.impact: Direct food waste reduction — saves ~€700/year if done regularly

actions.title: Download the BirdWatch Ireland app and log one bird sighting this week
actions.desc: The app is free and lets you identify and record birds. Every sighting contributes to national population monitoring data used by scientists and policymakers.
actions.impact: Supports citizen science and biodiversity monitoring

actions.title: Let a patch of your garden or outdoor space grow a little wilder this month
actions.desc: Stop cutting one corner of the lawn, or leave a strip along a fence uncut. Even small wild patches support the insects that birds — including migrants — depend on for food.
actions.impact: Supports local insect and bird populations

actions.title: Ask your GP about green prescribing or local nature-based wellbeing programmes
actions.desc: Look up local programmes at mentalhealthireland.ie or greencareireland.ie. Nature-based activities are increasingly recognised as effective treatment — not just lifestyle extras.
actions.impact: Nature access is a public health issue

actions.title: Walk or cycle to your next GP or pharmacy visit if it is under 3 km
actions.desc: Short car trips under 3 km produce disproportionately high emissions per km because the engine never warms up fully. Walking or cycling is better for you and the air around the clinic.
actions.impact: Short trips saved = disproportionate emissions reduction

actions.title: Swap one product in your weekly shop for a Fairtrade alternative
actions.desc: Coffee, tea, chocolate or bananas are the easiest starting points — all widely available in Irish supermarkets with the Fairtrade mark. Usually the same price or very close.
actions.impact: Supports sustainable farming in climate-vulnerable regions

actions.title: Check if your workplace uses Fairtrade tea and coffee
actions.desc: If not, suggest it — it is usually the same price and some suppliers provide free point-of-sale materials. One workplace switch multiplies the effect across many people.

actions.title: Try one meal this week built around Irish-grown vegetables or legumes instead of meat
actions.desc: Legumes like lentils and beans fix nitrogen naturally, reducing the need for chemical fertiliser. They are cheap, filling and widely available. A simple dahl or bean stew works perfectly.
actions.impact: Plant-based meals save 2–5 kg CO₂ vs beef equivalent

actions.title: Leave a corner of your outdoor space uncut this month
actions.desc: If you have a garden, leave one corner uncut until the end of May. Ground-nesting insects and small mammals use rough grass — and whatever flowers appear will support pollinators.
actions.impact: Supports local insect and bird populations

actions.title: Visit one of Ireland's national parks or nature reserves this weekend
actions.desc: Ireland has 6 national parks — Killarney, Glenveagh, Connemara, Ballycroy, The Burren and Wicklow Mountains. All are free to enter. Find events near you at biodiversityweek.ie.
actions.impact: Zero carbon + builds connection to nature

actions.title: Calculate your household carbon footprint together
actions.desc: Use the free calculator at myclimate.org — it takes about 10 minutes as a family and shows clearly where your biggest impact areas are. Knowing is the first step.

actions.title: Download the free iNaturalist app and photograph one plant, bird or insect this week
actions.desc: iNaturalist identifies species from photos automatically and submits your record to national biodiversity databases. Every observation matters — especially outside the main cities.

actions.title: Check what biodiversity events are happening near you this week
actions.desc: Visit biodiversityweek.ie — events range from rockpool tours to moth nights to wildflower walks. Most are free and run by local naturalists, conservation groups and councils.
actions.impact: Builds knowledge and local connection to nature

actions.title: Try oat milk in your tea or coffee once this week
actions.desc: Irish brand Flahavan's now produces oat milk made from Irish-grown oats. One switch per day over a year saves roughly 50 to 100 kg CO₂. Most cafés and supermarkets stock it.
actions.impact: ~50–100 kg CO₂ saved per year if switched daily

actions.title: If you buy dairy, look for the Origin Green or organic label
actions.desc: Both indicate higher environmental standards. Organic dairy farms support significantly more biodiversity than conventional farms — more wildflowers, more insects, more birds.
actions.impact: Organic dairy supports significantly higher on-farm biodiversity

actions.title: Plant one bee-friendly plant this week
actions.desc: Lavender, borage, phacelia or any native wildflower — all available in Irish garden centres from May. A single lavender plant in flower can attract dozens of bee species. Even a small pot on a windowsill counts.

actions.title: Stop cutting one patch of grass for the rest of May
actions.desc: Let whatever grows there flower. Dandelions, clover and daisies are among the most important food sources for bees — and they grow themselves. No effort, big impact.
actions.impact: Provides immediate food source for wild bees

actions.title: Sign your organisation or community group up to the All-Ireland Pollinator Plan
actions.desc: It is free and takes 10 minutes at pollinators.ie. Every signed-up organisation commits to at least one action for pollinators — from changing mowing schedules to planting wildflowers.

actions.title: Cook one meal this week using a vegetable or grain you have never tried before
actions.desc: Try pearl barley, spelt, or a heritage vegetable from a local market or farm shop. Eating more variety directly supports demand for agricultural biodiversity.

actions.title: Visit the Irish Seed Savers Association online
actions.desc: Visit irishseedsavers.ie — you can order heritage Irish seeds by post and grow them at home. Every garden growing heritage varieties helps preserve Ireland's food biodiversity.
actions.impact: Preserves genetic diversity in Irish food crops

actions.title: Share one thing you learned this week about Irish biodiversity with someone
actions.desc: A friend, a colleague, or a post on social media. Talking about biodiversity is one of the most effective ways to build the social momentum for change. Most people care — they just do not know the facts.
actions.impact: Social multiplier effect — builds climate conversation culture

actions.title: Contact your local council and ask what they are doing for the All-Ireland Pollinator Plan
actions.desc: Every council in Ireland has signed up to the Pollinator Plan. Ask what actions they are taking in your area — changing mowing schedules, planting wildflowers, or creating pollinator corridors. Your question matters.
actions.impact: Local action is where biodiversity policy becomes real

actions.title: Attend or follow Africa Day events in Dublin or your local area
actions.desc: Many Africa Day events include climate and environment themes. Check africaday.ie for events near you this weekend. Understanding the human face of climate change is the first step to caring about it.

actions.title: Choose Fairtrade or direct trade coffee, tea or chocolate this week
actions.desc: Check where your daily coffee comes from. Fairtrade and direct trade products support farmers on the frontline of climate change — and are widely available in Irish supermarkets and cafés.
actions.impact: Supports climate-resilient farming in vulnerable regions

actions.title: Next time you are near a river or lake, stop and watch for a few minutes
actions.desc: Otters are most active at dawn and dusk — and are more common than most people realise, even in urban rivers. Knowing what lives in your local waterway is the first step to caring about it.

actions.title: Never pour cooking oil, medicines or cleaning products down the drain
actions.desc: They travel directly into waterways and affect everything living there. Cooking oil can be left to cool and disposed of in the bin. Medicines can be returned to any pharmacy in Ireland.
actions.impact: Prevents direct pollution of local waterways

actions.title: Do a 10-minute litter pick on your nearest beach, riverbank or canal path
actions.desc: Bring a bag and pick up what you find. Clean Coasts Ireland runs regular organised beach cleans — find one near you at cleancoasts.org. They provide bags and gloves.
actions.impact: Direct environmental impact — prevents marine pollution

actions.title: Switch from plastic bags to reusable bags permanently if you have not already
actions.desc: Check your freezer bags, sandwich bags and cling film too — all have reusable or compostable alternatives now available in Irish supermarkets. Single-use plastic bags are among the most common items in Irish marine surveys.
actions.impact: Reduces one of the most harmful forms of marine plastic

actions.title: Read about the Irish Supreme Court climate case
actions.desc: Visit friendsoftheirishenvironment.org — it shows what citizens can achieve when they hold governments accountable. Understanding the case takes about 5 minutes and changes how you see climate policy.

actions.title: Write to or email your local TD about one specific climate or nature issue
actions.desc: You do not need to be an expert — just a constituent. Find your TD at oireachtas.ie and write one short, specific, polite message about something you care about. TDs respond to constituent contact.

actions.title: Read Trócaire's annual report on climate and conflict
actions.desc: Visit trocaire.org — it shows the real human stories behind the data on climate displacement and conflict. Ireland's overseas aid work is directly connected to climate resilience in the most vulnerable regions.
actions.impact: Builds understanding of climate justice and global impact

actions.title: Next time you see a conflict or displacement story in the news, look up whether climate is a contributing factor
actions.desc: Use reliefweb.int or ceobs.org to find the environmental context behind global crises. It usually is a factor — and knowing that changes how you understand the news.
actions.impact: Awareness — connecting climate to global events

actions.title: Check the sustainability label on seafood before you buy it this week
actions.desc: Look for the Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) label on fish. It is the most widely recognised standard for sustainably caught seafood and is available in most Irish supermarkets.

actions.title: Reduce one plastic item you use this week
actions.desc: Plastic pollution is one of the top threats to marine ecosystems. Refuse a plastic bag, straw, or coffee cup lid this week and replace it with a reusable alternative.
actions.impact: Reduces plastic entering Irish waterways and the ocean

actions.title: Check if your electricity supplier offers a green tariff
actions.desc: Many Irish energy suppliers now offer tariffs where your electricity is matched to renewable generation. Switching can take less than 10 minutes online and often costs the same or less.

actions.title: Look into the SEAI home upgrade grant scheme
actions.desc: Grants of up to EUR 1,800 for solar panels and up to EUR 12,500 for heat pumps are available in 2026. Even reading through the options at seai.ie is a useful first step.
actions.impact: Home upgrades can cut heating emissions by up to 70%

actions.title: Try cycling or walking for one journey this week you would usually make by car
actions.desc: Any trip under 3km is often faster by bike once you factor in parking. Give it one try this week and notice how you feel.

actions.title: Turn your heating thermostat down by one degree
actions.desc: Reducing your thermostat by just one degree can cut your heating costs by around 10% and reduce your home's carbon emissions noticeably over a full year.

actions.title: Register your action on the UNEP global map
actions.desc: Visit worldenvironmentday.global -- it takes two minutes to register a pledge and join a global movement of people acting on climate.

actions.title: Share one climate fact with someone today using #NowForClimate
actions.desc: Pick the most surprising thing you learned from today's challenge and share it with one person, in conversation or on social media. Breaking the spiral of silence on climate is one of the most powerful things you can do.

actions.title: Find a Great Big Green Week event near you
actions.desc: Visit greatbiggreenweek.com to find a local event this week -- from beach cleans to sustainability talks. Community action on climate and nature is happening all around Ireland right now.

actions.title: Use the Re-Turn app to return your bottles and cans this week
actions.desc: Find your nearest return point and bring your plastic bottles and aluminium cans. You get your deposit back, and the materials stay in the circular economy and out of the ocean.

actions.title: Suggest a walk or outdoor lunch to a male colleague, friend, or family member this week
actions.desc: You do not need to make it about mental health -- just the walk. Getting outside together is one of the simplest and most effective things two people can do for each other.
actions.impact: Zero carbon and significant wellbeing benefit

actions.title: Visit a green space near you that you have never been to before
actions.desc: Most Irish towns and cities have parks, canal walks, or nature areas within easy reach. Find one you have never visited and go this week.

actions.title: Find a Great Big Green Week event and sign up
actions.desc: Visit greatbiggreenweek.com -- events range from beach cleans to sustainability workshops and community tree planting. Most are free.

actions.title: Contact your local authority and ask what community climate support is available
actions.desc: Most local councils in Ireland now have a climate action officer and community grants. A simple email or phone call can open up support you did not know existed.

actions.title: Plan a visit to one of Ireland's six national parks this summer
actions.desc: Killarney, Glenveagh, Connemara, Ballycroy, Wicklow Mountains, and the Burren. All are free to enter. Pick the one closest to you and put a date in the diary.
actions.impact: Zero carbon and significant wellbeing benefit

actions.title: Look up social prescribing services in your local area through the HSE
actions.desc: If you or someone you know is struggling with stress or low mood, nature-based activities are increasingly available through GPs and community health networks. Ask about it.
actions.impact: Nature access is a public health issue

actions.title: Share one thing you did or learned during Great Big Green Week
actions.desc: Tell a friend, post on social media, or bring it up at work. Talking openly about what you are doing on sustainability is one of the most effective ways to normalise it for others.

actions.title: Sign up to the Clean Coasts network
actions.desc: Clean Coasts Ireland connects thousands of volunteers around Ireland's coastline. Signing up takes two minutes and keeps you connected to marine action all year round.

actions.title: Use the SEAI solar calculator to estimate savings at your address
actions.desc: The free calculator at seai.ie estimates generation, savings, and payback time for any Irish address. It takes about five minutes.

actions.title: Refuse a plastic straw or lid the next time you buy a drink
actions.desc: Most cafes and takeaways will happily skip the straw or plastic lid if you ask. It takes one second and removes one piece of plastic from circulation.

actions.title: Report any sea turtle sighting off the Irish coast
actions.desc: If you spot a sea turtle off the Irish coast, report it to the Irish Whale and Dolphin Group at iwdg.ie. Every sighting contributes to national marine monitoring.
actions.impact: Supports citizen science and marine conservation

actions.title: Switch to peat-free compost this year
actions.desc: Peat-free compost is now widely available in Irish garden centres and supermarkets. It performs just as well and avoids contributing to peatland destruction.

actions.title: Support the Irish Peatland Conservation Council
actions.desc: Visit ipcc.ie to learn about bog restoration in Ireland and how to get involved. You can adopt a bog, join a guided walk, or donate to restoration work.
actions.impact: Peatland restoration stores and sequesters carbon

actions.title: Check if your electricity supplier is sourcing wind power
actions.desc: Look for a green tariff if your current supplier is not using renewable sources. Switching takes about 10 minutes and supports demand for wind energy.

actions.title: Write to your local TD about offshore wind planning in your area
actions.desc: Offshore wind projects are being delayed by planning and grid connection issues. A short, polite message to your TD asking about local progress takes five minutes and makes a difference.

actions.title: Check your fridge before your next food shop and plan meals around what is already there
actions.desc: Before you go shopping this week, open your fridge and write a list based only on what you actually need. Stick to it. It takes five minutes and saves money.
actions.impact: Could save EUR 700 and significant CO2 per year

actions.title: Freeze bread, meat, or leftovers before they go off
actions.desc: Most foods can be frozen before they spoil. Bread, meat, cheese, and cooked leftovers all freeze well. Freeze today rather than bin tomorrow.

actions.title: Plan a visit to Killarney National Park or Glengarriff Woods
actions.desc: Both are free to enter and contain Ireland's finest surviving rainforest. Bring waterproofs and look for the layers of moss, lichen, and fern that cover every surface.
actions.impact: Builds connection to Ireland's rarest habitat

actions.title: Support the Wild Atlantic Rainforest Restoration Project
actions.desc: Visit hometree.ie to learn about rainforest restoration in Ireland and how to contribute. Every native tree planted is a step toward restoring this ancient landscape.
actions.impact: Native woodland restoration stores carbon and supports biodiversity

actions.title: Use the SEAI solar calculator to estimate what a system could generate at your address
actions.desc: The free tool at seai.ie takes about five minutes and gives you a personalised estimate of generation, savings, and grant eligibility.
actions.impact: Planning step toward ~1 tonne CO2 saving per year

actions.title: Look into a community energy project if solar is not right for your home
actions.desc: Not every home is suitable for rooftop solar. Community energy projects allow groups to share the benefits of renewables without individual rooftop installation. Visit communitypower.ie.
actions.impact: Supports renewable energy in your community

actions.title: Check if there is a community energy project in your area
actions.desc: Visit communitypower.ie to find active projects near you or explore how to start one. Community groups, GAA clubs, and housing estates have all successfully launched projects.
actions.impact: Community renewables displace fossil fuel generation

actions.title: Share this challenge with a neighbour and start a conversation about community energy
actions.desc: Most community energy projects started with one person asking one neighbour a question. You do not need technical expertise -- just curiosity and a willingness to start.

actions.title: Try using public transport or a bicycle for one car journey this week
actions.desc: The most sustainable vehicle is the one you do not use. Even replacing one car journey per week with public transport or cycling adds up to a significant annual saving.

actions.title: Write down one thing you have changed or learned about sustainability in the first half of 2026
actions.desc: Even a single note in your phone counts. Reflecting on what you have done so far makes it more likely you will keep going. Progress, not perfection.

actions.title: Sign up for Plastic Free July starting next week
actions.desc: Visit plasticfreejuly.org and choose your level of challenge for July. The campaign has over 100 million participants and makes it much easier to cut single-use plastic when you are doing it alongside millions of others.
actions.impact: Reduces single-use plastic consumption throughout July

actions.title: Sign up for the official Plastic Free July challenge
actions.desc: Visit plasticfreejuly.org -- it is free, takes one minute, and connects you to over 100 million people doing the same thing. Choose your level: one item, the top four, or all single-use plastic.
actions.impact: Commits you to a month of reduced plastic use

actions.title: Tell one other person about Plastic Free July today
actions.desc: Behaviour change is easier when you do it with someone else. Tell a friend, colleague, or family member and invite them to join you.

actions.title: Return your plastic bottles and cans this week
actions.desc: Use the Re-Turn app or website to find your nearest return point. You get your deposit back, and the materials stay in the circular economy and out of the ocean.
actions.impact: Reduces plastic entering the marine environment

actions.title: Pick up three pieces of litter on your next walk near water
actions.desc: It takes 30 seconds and removes potential marine pollution directly. Rivers, canals, and coastal paths are where land-based plastic most often enters the sea.

actions.title: Count how many single-use plastic bags come into your home this week
actions.desc: Just count them. Awareness is the first step. Then aim to cut that number in half next week by keeping a reusable bag in your car, bag, or coat pocket.
actions.impact: Builds awareness of personal plastic use

actions.title: Share Ireland's plastic bag levy story with someone outside Ireland
actions.desc: Most people outside Ireland do not know it started here. It is a great example of a policy that actually worked and a conversation starter about what is possible.

actions.title: Choose loose fruit and vegetables instead of pre-packaged ones this week
actions.desc: Loose produce is almost always available in Irish supermarkets and costs the same or less. It is one of the simplest packaging reductions you can make every single week.

actions.title: Check mywaste.ie before putting something in the recycling bin
actions.desc: Not all plastic is recyclable. Black plastic trays, crisp packets, and stretchy film cannot go in the household recycling. Check before you bin.

actions.title: Share the fact that Ireland has rainforest with one person today
actions.desc: Most Irish people have never heard of temperate rainforest. Sharing the story builds awareness and support for conservation. You can start by sharing today's challenge.
actions.impact: Builds awareness of Ireland's rarest habitat

actions.title: Wash synthetic clothing less frequently and at lower temperatures
actions.desc: Synthetic fibres like polyester and nylon shed microplastics with every wash. Washing at 30C less often significantly reduces the amount released into waterways.
actions.impact: Reduces microplastic pollution and energy use

actions.title: Check personal care products for microbeads using the Beat the Microbead app
actions.desc: Download the free Beat the Microbead app (beatthemicrobead.org) to scan products and identify those containing intentionally added plastic particles.

actions.title: Bring your reusable coffee cup every day this week
actions.desc: Put it next to your keys or bag tonight so you cannot leave without it tomorrow. If you forget it, skip the takeaway coffee -- that is the challenge.
actions.impact: Removes ~365 disposable cups per year from circulation

actions.title: Refuse a straw, lid, or single-use cutlery you do not need this week
actions.desc: When ordering food or a drink, simply say you do not need the straw or plastic lid. One word saves one item of plastic every time.

actions.title: Choose loose fruit and vegetables instead of pre-packaged options this weekend
actions.desc: Most Irish supermarkets stock loose produce that is the same quality and price as packaged alternatives. Making this swap every week removes a significant amount of packaging over a year.

actions.title: Bring your own container to a deli or takeaway that allows it
actions.desc: Many Irish delis and cafes now accept customer containers. Ask first -- most are happy to oblige and some offer a small discount.

actions.title: Find your nearest zero-waste or refill shop
actions.desc: Search 'zero waste shop' with your town name. Many Irish towns now have them. Try buying one product -- washing-up liquid, shampoo, or oats -- without packaging this week.

actions.title: Try one meal this week using only ingredients without plastic packaging
actions.desc: Plan a meal using loose produce, glass jars, or tins. Pasta with tomatoes from a glass jar and loose onions and garlic is a good starting point.

actions.title: Check your bathroom cabinet for products containing microbeads
actions.desc: Look for 'polyethylene' or 'polypropylene' in the ingredients list of scrubs, toothpaste, or face washes. If present, switch to a product without them. Use the Beat the Microbead app to scan products.

actions.title: Write to your local supermarket asking them to expand loose or refillable options
actions.desc: Supermarkets respond to customer feedback. A short email asking for more loose produce or refill stations takes five minutes and contributes to retail change.

actions.title: Carry a reusable cup today
actions.desc: If you are going to a coffee shop, bring your cup. If you forget it, drink in rather than taking away. One cup per day adds up to around 250 disposable cups per year.
actions.impact: Removes ~250 disposable cups per year from circulation

actions.title: Report a litter blackspot in your area
actions.desc: Contact your local council or use the Litter.ie reporting tool. Local authorities are required to respond to litter reports. Your report matters.

actions.title: Before you bin something today, check mywaste.ie to make sure it belongs in recycling
actions.desc: One contaminated load can cause an entire truck of recycling to go to landfill. Checking takes 30 seconds and makes the recycling system work properly.

actions.title: Rinse containers before putting them in the recycling bin
actions.desc: Food residue contaminates other materials in the recycling stream. A quick rinse of yogurt pots, sauce jars, and tins is all that is needed.

actions.title: Write down which plastic swaps you have managed to make this month
actions.desc: Even a note in your phone counts. Reflecting on what you have done makes it more likely you will keep going after July ends.

actions.title: Share your Plastic Free July experience with one person
actions.desc: Tell someone what you have changed this month. Research shows that talking about behaviour change with others is one of the most effective ways to sustain it.

actions.title: If you know a farmer, ask how agricultural plastic is managed on their farm
actions.desc: It starts a useful conversation and may help a farmer find options they were not aware of, such as county collection schemes or Repak take-back programmes.
actions.impact: Raises awareness of agricultural plastic waste

actions.title: Avoid buying products that use excessive secondary plastic packaging
actions.desc: Secondary packaging -- shrink wrap, plastic trays holding multiple items -- is one of the least necessary forms. Choosing products without it sends a market signal to producers.

actions.title: When you see 'biodegradable' on a product, ask what conditions are required
actions.desc: Most 'biodegradable' plastics only biodegrade in industrial composting facilities, not in home compost or the environment. If the conditions are not specified, treat the claim with scepticism.

actions.title: Write to one brand you buy from asking what they are doing to reduce single-use plastic
actions.desc: Companies track customer feedback. A short email from a customer carries more weight than you might think, especially when combined with others asking the same question.

actions.title: Find your nearest refill shop and try buying one product without packaging
actions.desc: Search 'zero waste shop' or 'refill shop' with your town name. Many now stock washing-up liquid, shampoo, conditioner, and dry goods. Try one product this week.

actions.title: Carry a refillable water bottle this week and use a public refill point
actions.desc: Use the Tap app to find a free water refill point near you. It is free, takes no extra time, and removes one plastic bottle per use from circulation.

actions.title: Ask your workplace about its policy on single-use plastic
actions.desc: Does your canteen, office kitchen, or event catering use single-use plastic? A simple question to facilities management or the sustainability team can start a useful conversation.

actions.title: Choose to buy from one business this week that is making a genuine effort to reduce packaging
actions.desc: Vote with your wallet. Supporting businesses that have already made changes encourages others to follow. Look for reusable cup discounts, loose produce, and plastic-free shelves.

actions.title: Plan a visit to a green space, forest, beach, or national park this weekend
actions.desc: Leave the phone behind if you can. Walk slowly. Notice what you see, hear, and smell. Research shows that even 20 minutes makes a measurable difference to your mood.
actions.impact: Zero carbon and significant wellbeing benefit

actions.title: Invite one other person to join you outdoors
actions.desc: Connection in nature is doubly beneficial. Suggest an outdoor walk, cycle, or park visit to someone you care about this week.

actions.title: Learn about Ireland's saltmarshes and seagrass beds
actions.desc: Visit npws.ie to learn about Ireland's coastal habitats. Saltmarshes are found in sheltered bays around Ireland and are some of the most carbon-dense ecosystems in the country.
actions.impact: Builds awareness of Irish blue carbon ecosystems

actions.title: Choose only certified sustainable seafood this week
actions.desc: Sustainable fishing practices protect the coastal ecosystems -- including seagrass beds and mangrove-adjacent habitats -- that are critical for blue carbon storage. Look for the MSC label.

actions.title: Support WWF's tiger conservation work
actions.desc: Visit wwf.ie to learn about tiger conservation and how your support reaches field protection teams. Even a small monthly donation funds habitat protection and anti-poaching work.
actions.impact: Supports habitat protection for endangered species

actions.title: Reflect on what biodiversity means to you and share it with one person
actions.desc: Biodiversity is abstract until it is personal. Think about a wild animal, plant, or landscape you love and share why it matters to you. Personal stories are the most powerful catalyst for change.

actions.title: Use a pocket ashtray instead of dropping the butt
actions.desc: If you smoke or vape, small tin or pouch ashtrays are cheap and stop butts washing into drains and rivers.
actions.impact: Reduces microplastic and toxin pollution in waterways

actions.title: Pick up 3 cigarette butts next time you're out for a walk
actions.desc: It sounds small, but every butt kept out of a drain is one less source of microplastics and chemicals in the water.
actions.impact: Prevents chemical leaching into local water systems

actions.title: Pick one new habit and attach it to something you already do
actions.desc: Like bringing a reusable cup when you get coffee, or switching off devices before bed.

actions.title: Do a 10-minute home energy check
actions.desc: Walk around your home and note anything using energy needlessly. Most fixes take minutes.
actions.impact: Up to 100 kg CO2/year if acted on

actions.title: Learn to identify 3 native hedgerow species near you
actions.desc: Blackthorn, hawthorn and hazel are common in Irish hedges.
actions.impact: Builds awareness of local biodiversity loss

actions.title: Support a local hedgerow or tree planting scheme
actions.desc: One mature hedge can support hundreds of species.
actions.impact: Sequesters roughly 50% more carbon than a similar area of forestry

actions.title: Fix a dripping tap this week
actions.desc: A single dripping tap can waste over 5,000 litres of water a year.
actions.impact: Saves thousands of litres of treated water annually

actions.title: Take one minute off your shower
actions.desc: Small change, adds up fast across a household.
actions.impact: Can save over 5,000 litres per person per year

actions.title: Report white-tailed eagle sightings if you spot one
actions.desc: Golden Eagle Trust and NPWS track sightings to monitor the population.
actions.impact: Supports population monitoring and conservation research

actions.title: Support an elephant or raptor conservation charity
actions.desc: Small, regular donations fund habitat protection and anti-poaching work.
actions.impact: Funds habitat protection for endangered species

actions.title: Plan one Irish trip this year instead of flying
actions.desc: Explore a county you've never visited by train or car.
actions.impact: Avoids the highest-carbon part of most holidays

actions.title: If you do fly, choose direct routes
actions.desc: Layovers add extra take-offs and landings, the most fuel-heavy part of a flight.
actions.impact: Cuts unnecessary take-off and landing emissions

actions.title: Check the EPA's bathing water status before you swim
actions.desc: Takes a minute, tells you what you're getting into.
actions.impact: Protects your own health and highlights pollution hotspots

actions.title: Cut back on garden fertiliser this month
actions.desc: Excess nutrients feed the same algae blooms affecting places like Lough Neagh.

actions.title: Learn what Bord na Móna's rehabilitation programme covers
actions.desc: It's restoring 33,000 hectares of former industrial peatland across 82 midland bogs, over half already done.
actions.impact: Supports Ireland's largest peatland carbon restoration programme

actions.title: Visit a restored bog walk near you
actions.desc: Many restored midland bogs now have boardwalks and trails, a good way to see peatland recovery firsthand.
actions.impact: Builds public support for peatland restoration

actions.title: Check for a uniform swap or secondhand scheme at school
actions.desc: Many parent associations run informal swaps, worth asking before buying new.
actions.impact: Extends the useful life of school uniforms

actions.title: Reuse stationery and bags from last year where you can
actions.desc: A working schoolbag or pencil case doesn't need replacing just because it's a new year.
actions.impact: Reduces demand for new school supplies

actions.title: Check what share of your electricity supplier's mix is renewable
actions.desc: Most Irish suppliers publish a fuel mix disclosure, worth a look.

actions.title: Time energy-heavy tasks for windier days if you can
actions.desc: Ireland's grid runs cleanest when wind output is high, small timing shifts help.
actions.impact: Shifts demand toward cleaner grid periods

actions.title: Use your brown bin for garden and food waste this BBQ season
actions.desc: Grass clippings and food scraps belong there, not the general bin.
actions.impact: Diverts waste from landfill to composting

actions.title: Portion your BBQ food a little more carefully
actions.desc: Overcatering is one of the most common causes of summer food waste. A rough headcount plan helps.
actions.impact: Reduces food waste at the source

actions.title: Join a bat walk this month
actions.desc: Many local heritage or biodiversity groups run evening bat walks with bat detectors.
actions.impact: Builds appreciation and awareness of local biodiversity

actions.title: Leave a corner of your garden a little wild
actions.desc: Long grass and native shrubs attract the insects bats feed on.
actions.impact: Supports local insect and bat populations

actions.title: Let one patch of your garden or green space grow wild this month
actions.desc: Late summer wildflowers like ivy and heather are a vital late-season food source for bees.
actions.impact: Supports pollinator food sources before winter

actions.title: Check if your workplace or community group is on the AIPP list
actions.desc: Businesses, schools and community groups can sign up to take specific pollinator-friendly actions.

actions.title: Try repairing one item before replacing it
actions.desc: A patch, a stitch or a cobbler visit often costs far less than buying new.
actions.impact: Extends the useful life of existing garments

actions.title: Drop unwanted textiles at a proper collection point, not the general bin
actions.desc: Textile banks and charity shops keep clothing in reuse rather than landfill.
actions.impact: Diverts textiles from landfill into reuse

actions.title: Learn if your area has a local coastal or flood risk plan
actions.desc: Local authority websites often have flood risk maps, worth checking if you're near the coast or a river.
actions.impact: Builds awareness of local climate risk

actions.title: Support dune and coastal habitat restoration where you can
actions.desc: Healthy dune systems act as a natural buffer against erosion and storm surges.

actions.title: Check in on elderly or vulnerable neighbours during a heatwave
actions.desc: Heat-related illness is a real and growing risk, even in Ireland's traditionally mild summers.

actions.title: Learn your area's wildfire risk if you're near forest or gorse land
actions.desc: Ireland has seen its own gorse and forest fires in dry spells, knowing the risk helps you act early.

actions.title: Follow research updates from Irish biodiversity conferences
actions.desc: Universities and NPWS often share key findings publicly after events like this.

actions.title: Share one surprising biodiversity fact with someone this week
actions.desc: Awareness is often the first step toward support for conservation funding and policy.
actions.impact: Builds broader public support for conservation

actions.title: Do a wardrobe audit this weekend
actions.desc: Count how many items you haven't worn in a year, a good sign of what you could sell, swap or donate.
actions.impact: Highlights overconsumption without needing a purchase

actions.title: Look up your nearest clothes swap or charity shop
actions.desc: Ireland has a strong charity shop culture, check what's already out there before buying new.
actions.impact: Extends the useful life of existing garments

actions.title: Take the Second-Hand September pledge
actions.desc: Commit to buying nothing new this month. Try a charity shop, swap, or online secondhand marketplace first.
actions.impact: Avoids emissions from new garment production

actions.title: Sell or donate 5 items you no longer wear
actions.desc: Someone else's secondhand find starts with your own wardrobe.
actions.impact: Extends the useful life of existing garments

actions.title: Try one organic swap in your weekly shop
actions.desc: Pick one item, maybe your fruit and veg, and go organic for a week.

actions.title: Look for the EU organic logo when shopping
actions.desc: The green leaf logo means the product meets strict EU organic farming standards.
actions.impact: Helps identify verified organic produce quickly

actions.title: Walk or cycle the school run at least once this week
actions.desc: Even one day makes a difference to both traffic and air quality outside the school gates.
actions.impact: Cuts short-trip car emissions near schools

actions.title: Check if there's a Safe Routes scheme near your school
actions.desc: See what's planned or already built nearby, and support it if there's a local consultation.

actions.title: Check your attic and wall insulation
actions.desc: Poor insulation is one of the biggest reasons Irish homes waste heat. SEAI grants can cover a large share of upgrade costs.
actions.impact: Cuts heat loss and heating-related emissions

actions.title: Bleed your radiators before the cold sets in
actions.desc: Trapped air makes radiators work harder for less heat. A five-minute job.

actions.title: Check if smoky coal or turf is legal to burn in your area
actions.desc: Rules have been tightening across Ireland, a quick check avoids an unknowing breach.

actions.title: Get your solid fuel stove serviced
actions.desc: A poorly maintained stove burns less efficiently and produces more smoke.

actions.title: Watch for a murmuration at dusk this month
actions.desc: Starlings gather at reliable roost sites just before sunset. BirdWatch Ireland lists known spots.
actions.impact: Builds appreciation and awareness of local biodiversity

actions.title: Record a wildlife sighting on a citizen science app
actions.desc: Apps like iNaturalist or BirdTrack let you log what you see, and the data genuinely helps researchers.
actions.impact: Supports species and seasonal monitoring data

actions.title: Add one seasonal Irish item to your shop this week
actions.desc: Look for Irish apples, blackberries or kale instead of imported alternatives, often cheaper too.

actions.title: Check the origin label before you buy fruit and veg
actions.desc: Only takes a second, and builds the habit of noticing where your food comes from.

actions.title: Reach out to check in with someone today
actions.desc: A short message or call to someone you haven't spoken to in a while can matter more than you think.

actions.title: Take a 15-minute walk somewhere green
actions.desc: Doesn't need to be long or far. A local park, riverside path, or stretch of coast all count.

actions.title: Refuse single-use cutlery or straws this week
actions.desc: Say no when offered, or carry a small reusable set. Adds up over hundreds of takeaways a year.

actions.title: Do one plastic-free grocery shop
actions.desc: Choose loose fruit and veg, and packaging-free options where you can find them.

actions.title: Look up what Ireland's carbon tax actually funds
actions.desc: A few minutes on gov.ie shows exactly where the ring-fenced revenue goes.
actions.impact: Builds understanding of national climate policy

actions.title: Follow COP31 coverage as it happens
actions.desc: Following even a few days of real coverage builds a much clearer picture than headlines alone.

actions.title: Learn one action from Ireland's National Biodiversity Action Plan
actions.desc: A few minutes on npws.ie shows practical steps happening at national level.
actions.impact: Builds understanding of national biodiversity policy

actions.title: Support a local biodiversity project
actions.desc: From community gardens to local Tidy Towns biodiversity initiatives, small local efforts add up.
actions.impact: Supports local habitat and species protection

actions.title: Check your fridge and AC unit are properly serviced
actions.desc: Older units can still leak banned refrigerant gases if damaged or poorly maintained.
actions.impact: Prevents leaks of ozone-depleting and warming gases

actions.title: Learn one thing about an environmental success story
actions.desc: The ozone layer is proof that global cooperation works, a genuinely hopeful climate story to share.

actions.title: Swap one short car trip for walking or cycling this week
actions.desc: If it's under 5km, there's a good chance you could walk or cycle it just as easily.

actions.title: Check out Climate Carnival or a local Mobility Week event near you
actions.desc: Local events often include free bike checks, taster cycling sessions or public transport demos.
actions.impact: Builds engagement with local low-carbon transport options

actions.title: Try one bamboo product swap
actions.desc: Toothbrushes, socks and kitchen utensils are common starting points. Watch out for bamboo viscose fabric, it's heavily processed and loses much of the benefit.

actions.title: Look for FSC or verified sourcing on bamboo products
actions.desc: Not all bamboo is grown or processed responsibly. A recognised certification is a good way to check.

actions.title: Support Irish Aid or a climate justice charity
actions.desc: Groups like Trócaire work directly with communities facing the worst impacts.
actions.impact: Supports climate adaptation in vulnerable regions

actions.title: Leave the car home for one trip today
actions.desc: Walk, cycle or bus one journey you'd normally drive.
actions.impact: Cuts one day's worth of car emissions

actions.title: Check your local Local Link or bus route
actions.desc: Many areas have more options than people realise.
actions.impact: Builds awareness of low-carbon transport options

actions.title: Try a Leap Card or local transport app for a week
actions.desc: See how far a single card or app gets you across buses, trains and trams.

actions.title: Cycle or walk one journey you'd usually drive
actions.desc: Doesn't need to be your commute, even a short errand counts.

actions.title: Suggest a green idea at work this week
actions.desc: A bike rack, a recycling audit, small changes that also boost morale.

actions.title: Try one active or public transport commute this week
actions.desc: Even once counts.

actions.title: Check mywaste.ie for anything you're unsure about
actions.desc: Two minutes now saves a contaminated bin later.

actions.title: Make sure recycling is clean, dry and loose
actions.desc: Food residue and bagged items are common causes of rejected batches.

actions.title: Start a bottle jar at home
actions.desc: A few euro in deposits adds up fast, and none of it ends up as litter.
actions.impact: Diverts containers from landfill into the return stream

actions.title: Find your nearest Re-Turn point
actions.desc: Most supermarkets have a machine, many corner shops accept returns over the counter.

actions.title: Plan your meals before you shop this week
actions.desc: A rough list stops food going off before you get to it.

actions.title: Start composting food waste if you don't already
actions.desc: Composting cuts food waste's climate impact by more than 90% versus landfill.
actions.impact: Cuts methane emissions from landfilled food waste

actions.title: Choose products with less packaging, not just recyclable packaging
actions.desc: Less packaging beats recyclable packaging every time.
actions.impact: Cuts packaging waste at the source

actions.title: Rinse and dry your recycling before it goes out
actions.desc: A few seconds under the tap stops a whole batch getting contaminated.

actions.title: Switch to a certified sustainable coffee brand
actions.desc: Look for Rainforest Alliance or organic certification next time you buy beans or ground coffee.
actions.impact: Reduces water use and land pressure per kg of beans

actions.title: Replace one car journey with public transport this week
actions.desc: Even one return trip by bus or train instead of car saves roughly 50 kg CO₂ over the year if done weekly.
actions.impact: ~50 kg CO₂ saved/year if done weekly

actions.title: Try one lamb-free week this month
actions.desc: Lamb has one of the highest footprints of any meat. Swapping it for chicken or legumes makes a real difference.
actions.impact: ~28 kg CO₂ saved per kg avoided

actions.title: Buy your next pair of shoes second-hand or from a sustainable brand
actions.desc: Manufacturing one pair of leather shoes produces ~30 kg CO₂. Second-hand or vegan alternatives cut that dramatically.
actions.impact: Up to 30 kg CO₂ saved per pair

actions.title: Try one beef-free week
actions.desc: Beef is the highest-impact common food. Replacing it with chicken, fish or plant protein just once a week adds up.
actions.impact: ~60 kg CO₂ saved per kg avoided

actions.title: Keep your current phone for one more year
actions.desc: Manufacturing a new smartphone produces ~70 kg CO₂. The best phone for the planet is the one you already own.

actions.title: Buy your next bike second-hand
actions.desc: Manufacturing a new bicycle uses ~96 kg CO₂. Second-hand bikes cut that to near zero, and save money too.

actions.title: Choose a local or low-travel event for your next big trip
actions.desc: A single major sporting event visit can cost 125 kg CO₂. Choosing an event within driving distance makes a big difference.
actions.impact: ~125 kg CO₂ saved per trip avoided

actions.title: Repair or refurbish your laptop instead of buying new
actions.desc: A new laptop produces ~300 kg CO₂ in manufacturing alone. Most repairs cost a fraction of that, and extend its life by years.

actions.title: Replace one short-haul flight with a train or ferry
actions.desc: A return Dublin–Madrid flight produces ~550 kg CO₂. For journeys under 5–6 hours, train is usually feasible and far lower impact.

actions.title: Enable downloads instead of streaming this week
actions.desc: Streaming constantly uses data centres. Downloading music or videos on Wi-Fi, then watching offline, cuts that energy use significantly.
actions.impact: Part of your ~636 kg/year digital footprint

actions.title: Switch your dog to a lower-impact food brand
actions.desc: A dog's annual footprint is ~770 kg CO₂, mostly from meat-based food. Several brands now offer lower-carbon recipes with insect or plant protein.

actions.title: Plan your meals this week to reduce food waste
actions.desc: The average household wastes enough food to produce 1,600 kg CO₂ a year. A simple weekly plan and checking your fridge before shopping can cut that by half.

actions.title: Swap one beef meal a week for chicken, or for beans and lentils
actions.desc: A 200 g beef portion is 3,083 L; the same portion of chicken is 865 L. Biggest single lever in the whole dataset. One meal, not your whole diet.

actions.title: Eat what you buy: finish the cheese, the bread and the leftovers before they go off
actions.desc: A wasted 1 kg block of cheese throws away 3,178 L; a wasted 800 g loaf, 1,286 L. Food you already own is the cheapest water saving available.
actions.impact: 3,178 L per wasted kilo of cheese

actions.title: Get one more year out of the clothes you own before replacing them
actions.desc: One t-shirt is 2,495 L and one pair of jeans is 8,000 L. One garment not bought beats months of shorter showers.

actions.title: Turn the tap off while you brush
actions.desc: 12 L becomes 1 L, twice a day. Costs nothing, and it is about three t-shirts' worth of water a year.

actions.title: Take two minutes off your shower
actions.desc: A standard showerhead runs at 9 L a minute. Same order of magnitude as the toothbrush habit. Small, but it compounds daily.

actions.title: Fix the tap that drips
actions.desc: A slow drip is about 15 L a day. A ten-minute job that runs in the background for the rest of the year.
